note: Literature confirms lateral eversion of the lower eyelid with elongated palpebral fissures is a hallmark of Kabuki syndrome (KDM6A/KMT2D), making palpebral fissure morphology a plausible discriminator for KDM6B.

evidence.text: Kabuki syndrome features long palpebral fissures with lower lateral eyelid eversion, associated with variants in KMT2D or KDM6A.

source.title: Kabuki syndrome—clinical review with molecular aspects
source.quote: with long or wide palpebral fissures, lower lateral eyelid eversion, arched eyebrows with the lateral third dispersed

evidence.text: In a molecularly confirmed cohort of Kabuki syndrome patients, lateral eversion of the lower eyelid was documented in 26 out of 47 individuals.

source.title: Insights into the genotype–phenotype relationship of ocular manifestations in Kabuki syndrome
source.quote: comprised of lateral eversion of the lower eyelid (26/47)
